result.direction: Editorial magazine feature. Three variants considered: 1. Broadsheet Lead: oversized bilingual headline, annotated image, subscription rail; strongest for launch authority. 2. Archive Desk: article index first, cover image secondary; loses the decisive first-screen feature moment. 3. Critic's Notebook: dense text-led essay opening; loses image-caption rhythm and subscription visibility. Chosen: Broadsheet Lead because the brief needs long titles, captions, metadata, and one subscription action to feel like a real magazine launch feature.

hierarchy: Visual thesis: an independent architecture magazine launches through one composed feature spread, not a marketing hero.

Feature stream: lead article, two secondary article teasers, image captions, issue note, then subscription action repeated once at the natural end if needed.

Composition contract: focal element is the long bilingual title paired with the lead image/caption; first-screen occupancy about 65%; asymmetry is 7/5 with text dominant and image bleeding to one edge; dominant contrast is type size and editorial measure; quiet zone sits below the lead image before secondary stories.

immersive.artDirection: Visual thesis: motion makes the hinge positions and resulting light direction legible. Hero subject: modular desk lamp with recognizable hinge, shade, base, and cone of light. Camera: natural product perspective, medium-close, FOV about 38-42 degrees, target on the hinge, near/far kept tight to the product stage. Composition: lamp anchored right-center on wide screens with left DOM safe area; portrait shot centers hinge and shade. Lighting: soft top-left key to define the shade and hinge, restrained fill for readable hardware, subtle rim for silhouette separation, one shadow owner at most. Materials: lamp body and hinge lead, shade secondary, light cone/accent tertiary, matte stage last. Color pipeline: Linear-sRGB work, sRGB output, fixed tone mapping and exposure. Spatial type: meaningful text remains DOM-first; any world label is decorative or duplicated in DOM. Poster: desktop and portrait posters match the selected live camera and show hinge plus light direction.
qualityTiers: Poster: canvas not mounted or stopped; responsive poster at CSS resolution; baked shadow and light direction; DOM controls remain usable.
Low: DPR 1.0; lowest acceptable lamp LOD; blob/contact shadow only; no PostFX; minimal or no idle motion; hinge changes can step between verified poses.
Medium: DPR 1.0-1.5; medium LOD; one tight 1024 key shadow; only motivated light-cone effect; core hinge animation allowed when visible.
High: DPR capped at 2.0; high foreground LOD under 500k desktop visible triangles and under 100 draw calls; one tight 2048 key shadow; selective renderer-compatible PostFX only if frame budget holds.

Adaptation: start at Medium, degrade after roughly 2 seconds above 1.25x target frame time, upgrade only after roughly 8 seconds below 0.8x target, with 10 second cooldown and one central quality owner.
Pause: render loop, controls, mixers, animation, and measurement pause when offscreen or document-hidden.
immersive.fallback: GPU/WebGL unavailable, repeated context loss, Save-Data/low-end failure, or persistently unusable frame time shows the art-directed poster tier with the same DOM heading, copy, CTA, hinge-position controls, and shade detail. Loading must reserve layout and avoid a white flash. Verification status remains NOT_APPLICABLE (plan-only); first runnable build should capture wide, portrait, narrow, reduced-motion, poster, and GPU-fallback states.
touch: Surface: embedded hero, so `touch-action: pan-y`; vertical page scroll remains native.
Gesture role: tap selects hinge positions; optional horizontal drag may scrub between the three positions but must snap to verified states.
Thresholds: touch drag starts after about 10-12 CSS pixels; taps commit only when distance and duration stay below project limits.
Pointer capture: capture on valid pointerdown, commit on pointerup, and treat pointercancel, lostpointercapture, blur, and visibilitychange as aborts.
Pinch/zoom: no required pinch in the hero; provide DOM view controls instead of depending on multipoint gestures.
Hover fallback: hover highlights only on fine pointers; coarse pointers and keyboard focus use the same DOM-selected state with visible pressed controls.

Hero subject: recognizable backpack silhouette with front panel, straps, zipper/pocket structure, and fabric surface readable. Camera: natural product-view FOV around 35-42 degrees, medium framing, target on the upper front pocket for front view and strap plane for back view, tight near/far bounds. Composition: wide subject anchor right-center with left DOM safe area; portrait subject centered below controls. Lighting: soft top-left key, restrained fill, subtle rim for strap separation, at most one dynamic key shadow. Materials: fabric body is hero surface; straps, zipper, pull tabs, and hardware are secondary; selected hotspot is the only accent. Color output: Linear-sRGB work and sRGB output; tone mapping and exposure owned once. Spatial type: meaningful labels in DOM or Html hotspot only; no essential Text3D. Poster: separate front/back desktop and portrait stills matching the live view.
qualityTiers: Poster: no canvas mounted or stopped; responsive front/back poster images; DOM controls and shortlist remain active.
Low: active canvas at DPR 1; lowest acceptable LOD; baked/blob shadow; no postprocessing; limited or no idle motion.
Medium: initial tier; DPR 1 to 1.5; medium LOD; one tight 1024 key shadow; minimal motivated post/output pass only.
High: DPR capped at 2; foreground high LOD; one tight 2048 key shadow; selective postprocessing only if frame budget holds.

Budget: under 100 desktop and 50 mobile draw calls, under 500k desktop and 150k mobile visible triangles, textures no larger than 2048px, mobile DPR capped around 1.5, target 16.7ms frame time with degradation after sustained slow frames.

Adaptation: one quality owner controls DPR, LOD, shadows, postprocessing, idle loop, and poster fallback with hysteresis; pause render, controls, animation, and measurement when offscreen or document-hidden.
immersive.fallback: No WebGL, context loss, repeated crashes, reduced capability, or persistent unusable frame time switches to an art-directed poster tier. The semantic DOM still exposes the three fabric choices, front/back inspection, material information, Add to shortlist, and status feedback.
touch: Surface: embedded configurator section uses touch-action: pan-y so vertical page scroll remains native; scene drag is optional enhancement.
Thresholds: touch drag starts after roughly 10-12 CSS px; mouse/pen after roughly 6 CSS px; taps only commit when time and movement stay below limits.
Pointer capture: capture on permitted pointerdown, update during move, commit tap/selection only on pointerup, then release and clean up stored pointers.
Pinch/zoom: optional only if visible DOM zoom/reset controls also exist; clamp distance, keep the backpack inside the declared shot, and ignore synthetic clicks after pinch.
Hover fallback: hover can reveal emphasis only for fine pointers; tap and keyboard focus open the same material information panel.

Cancellation: pointercancel, lostpointercapture, window blur, tab switch, second-pointer interruption, or diagonal scroll aborts transient drag/pinch and never triggers Add to shortlist or changes committed selection.
